comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C35, C36, C38 regarding AMPK and PPARα molecular signaling. Both evaluations find the evidence compelling and well-supported, with peer reviewers noting the convergence of multiple approaches strengthens the conclusion.

Perfect agreement on claims C53, C54, C55 regarding ATP usage findings. Both evaluations accept the two-photon ATP imaging data as compelling evidence, with peer reviewers specifically endorsing the darkness control that strengthens interpretation.

Perfect agreement on claims C57, C58, C59 regarding visual coding and orientation tuning. Both evaluations find the calcium imaging data well-supported with appropriate methodology and no methodological concerns raised.

Both address claims C62, C63, C64, C65 regarding Bayes factor analysis, but with different evaluations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging appropriate statistical methods. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, noting limitations in sample size for direct comparison and that absence of significance doesn't prove absence of effects.

Perfect agreement on claims C10, C11, C66, C67, C96, C97 representing the main conclusions. Both evaluations strongly support the core finding of sex-specific differences in cortical energy regulation, with peer reviewers calling it 'compelling evidence' and 'well-supported.'

Perfect agreement on claims C60, C61 regarding behavioral state controls. Both evaluations endorse these controls as appropriate for addressing potential confounds from arousal or attention differences, strengthening the interpretation of genuine metabolic differences.

Both address leptin findings (C8, C9, C28) with SUPPORTED evaluations. OpenEval also includes C29, C30 regarding interpretation of leptin reflecting fat mass and female resistance to fat loss. Peer reviewers accept the leptin measurements as compelling evidence without concerns.

Partial overlap on food intake and body weight claims (C26, C27). OpenEval also addresses C25. Both evaluations support the findings, with peer reviewers implicitly accepting the differential food restriction protocol as appropriate for achieving comparable weight loss.

Both address RNA sequencing findings (C39-C44). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with adequate sample size. Peer review also SUPPORTED, treating transcriptomic data as strong evidence with no methodological concerns. OpenEval result also includes claims about specific pathways (not in peer result).

OpenEval addresses GSEA pathway enrichment claims (C45, C46, C47, C49) as SUPPORTED. Peer result R3 addresses broader RNA-seq findings including some pathway claims. Both evaluations accept the transcriptomic evidence, though OpenEval provides more specific evaluation of pathway enrichment data.

Both address claim C68 regarding alternative energy-saving strategies in females. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative interpretations not directly tested. Peer review also UNCERTAIN, noting lack of evidence that females are unimpacted in visually guided behaviors and treating this as hypothesis rather than demonstrated fact.
